toegepas.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
toegepas.na: in al hoe kleiner stukkies op
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'al hoe kleiner' is the more common, natural idiom for a gradual decrease; 'al kleiner' is correct but reads stiffer for Grade 6.
toegepas.fout: 'al kleiner' is the stiffer, bookish form of the gradual-increase idiom.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'al hoe kleiner' is the natural spoken Afrikaans idiom for a Grade 6 reader and the meaning is unchanged.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Subject-first order reads more naturally here and is easier for a Grade 6 learner; the protected wording that follows is untouched.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Fronting 'So 'n siekte' deliberately links back to the previous sentence; the proposal is a lateral reorder that loosens that link.

laat_vaar.voor: siek kan maak of kan doodmaak
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The repeated 'kan' is redundant; 'siek of dood kan maak' is shorter and more natural with the same meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: This is a glossary definition and the repeated 'kan' is correct Afrikaans, so there is no real fault to justify rewording it.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: los in die water op en versprei deur die water
laat_vaar_vorige.na: los in die water op en versprei daardeur
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Avoids repeating 'die water' twice in one short clause.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The repetition is mild and plain for Grade 6, while 'daardeur' is stiffer and can be read as 'as a result of that', which risks moving the meaning.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: wat te klein is om te sien en mense siek kan maak
laat_vaar_vorige.na: wat mense siek kan maak en te klein is om te sien
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The original can be misread as 'too small to see and to make people sick'; reordering removes the ambiguity without changing the meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The finite 'kan maak' already ties the second clause to 'wat', so the misreading is unlikely, and the original order keeps visibility first in line with the other two list items.
